subject: Post-demo: ScalableMed POC - quantization briefing & next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@scalablemed.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@scalablemed.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: ScalableMed POC - model fit & quantization discussion

Thanks again for your time today — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Recap from call
- Goal: 2-week evaluation of inference profiles on a representative clinical summarization workload (de-identified).
- Main success metrics: latency P95 < 400ms on 1k tokens, cost per 1k tokens under target, and tolerable downgrade in ROUGE-F1 (<= 2 points).
- Key concerns you raised: hallucination risk on rare entities and model regressions from quantization.

2) Recommended starting model variants (we’ll run the initial bench on your sample set):
- Alpine-13B-v1 (FP16 baseline) — balanced quality/throughput.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (AWQ profile) — lower cost, aggressive quantization.
- Alpine-33B-v0 (mixed-FP16) — higher quality baseline if needed.

3) Quantization profiles & what we’ll measure
- AWQ vs GPTQ: throughput, peak memory, and quality delta on your eval prompts.
- FP8 (experimental) for Alpine-13B: pros/cons on degradation vs latency gains.

Attachments I’m sharing: ScalableMed POC MAP (roadmap & responsibilities), initial prompt set we discussed, and a baseline benchmark CSV template. I’ve attached: scalablemed-poc-map.pdf, scalablemed-prompt-set-v1.jsonl, awq-vs-gptq-benchmarks.csv

Next steps
- You: confirm dataset delivery window (can be synthetic/de-identified) and point of contact for IT networking.
- Us: run initial onboarding bench and share a short report within 48-72 hours of receiving the sample set.

If that looks right I’ll book the environment and drop a HubSpot task (SM-2026-042).

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications before we hand over data: 

- For AWQ vs GPTQ, can you share example quality deltas on clinical summarization tasks (we care about entity-level recall more than ROUGE sometimes)? If you have per-entity precision/recall that’d be ideal.
- Is FP8 considered production-ready or just experimental in your stack? We need a recommendation we can operationalize over the next quarter.
- On prompt sets: can you include a few edge-case prompts (rare medication combinations) so we can gauge hallucination risk?

We can get a 5k de-identified sample set over to you by Monday — Rajiv will handle the logistics. Also looping in IT (it@scalablemed.com) for firewall/VPN requirements.

Olivia Park
Head of ML | ScalableMed

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@scalablemed.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@scalablemed.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: ScalableMed POC - model fit & quantization discussion

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround on samples. Short answers up-front, details below: 

- Per-entity quality: we’ll produce an entity-level precision/recall table for named entities and Rx codes. We’ll include difference vs FP16 baseline for AWQ and GPTQ. Expect the initial delta to be small on common entities and larger on low-frequency tokens — we’ll highlight those.
- FP8 status: FP8 is marked as "experimental" in our public profiles — it shows strong throughput gains for Alpine-13B-family in controlled tests but requires conservative rollout (can introduce small numeric instability on long-context KV cache ops). For a production POC we recommend starting with AWQ on Mistral-7B and Alpine-13B in GPTQ-light mode; evaluate FP8 only if AWQ/GPTQ don’t meet throughput targets.
- Prompt edge cases: included in scalablemed-prompt-set-v1.jsonl are 25 edge-case prompts (rare meds, concatenated histories, annotated entities). Please confirm if you want more.

I’ve kicked off an internal bench run and attached the preliminary CSV template (awq-vs-gptq-benchmarks.csv). We’ll populate it with your samples and provide the per-entity PR curves.

Logistics: can your IT open outbound to the following IP ranges and provide a hostname for SFTP? (I’ll follow up with a concise checklist.)

Proposed next milestone: once we have samples (Mon) we’ll deliver a 72-hour bench report and recommend a quantization profile for the 2-week POC.

Thanks —
Karthik

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 trade notes for ScalableMed

Internal notes to share with Olivia/Rajiv in the bench deliverable (summarized):

- Throughput (normalized tokens/sec on r5-32g equivalent): AWQ(Mistral-7B, awq) ~ 1.8x vs FP16 baseline; GPTQ-light(Alpine-13B) ~ 1.5x; FP8(Alpine-13B) ~ 2.4x but with occasional variance on long-context scenarios.
- Memory: AWQ provides the most consistent memory profile and is easiest to deploy across Dedicated pools. GPTQ can be smaller but sensitivity to kernel selection yields some variability.
- Quality impact (clinical summarization sample): measured delta vs FP16 baseline on our internal eval (entity-F1): AWQ ~ -0.8 to -1.6 pts on low-frequency entities; GPTQ-light ~ -0.4 to -1.0 pts; FP8 ~ -1.5 to -3.5 pts depending on tokenization edge cases.
- Recommendation: start with AWQ for Mistral-7B for cost-constrained paths and GPTQ-light for Alpine-13B when you need a closer quality match. Reserve FP8 for controlled phases and only after we validate stability on your longer-thread examples.

I’ll prep a one-page appendix (table + short methodology) for the deliverable. Also adding a quick checklist for production rollout (fallback to FP16, rollout canary, monitoring for entity-drop regressions).

—Lauren
Director, Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
